[Rating: 3/10] A game that offers players the opportunity to create satisfying turns, but then takes agency away by having your opponent often dictate where you play. You are then required to proceed through those dictations to unsatisfying ends. Such weaponization of agency can be done well (see the Field of the Cloth of Gold). Here it just completely makes the game unpleasant in a truly disjointed way.

[Rating: 4/10] Gatsby is a game about Gatsby, sorta, except it isn't about Gatsby, see, it's about cozying up to Gatsby, except that isn't something you do in the game. Also, parties.  Read my review here: https://spacebiff.com/2025/08/25/gatsby/

[Rating: 4/10] Initial Impressions: I was pretty underwhelmed by this game, though possibly because my opponent didn't block me that much. It felt like all the decisionmaking is in finetuning getting the bonus actions and switching the people aroind, but how to get them or when you want to switch things around is often fairly obvious. And each of the 3 regions are fairly boring in their base effects.  I think this game is supposed to have the bluffing be front and center of who was switched where, and then you are going more for this region now so that character must be this color. [Rating: 4/10] [b]Action selection duel game where you are trying to collect tiles by playing mini-games. This is very abstracted and good play seems to be on a very fine line[/b]  + Simple to read the game state; easy to learn  - Very abstract action selection and tempo game - No arc makes the game feel sluggish and boring - The connection mini-game seems unnecessarily complicated  Can't say this did anything for me. There's some racing and some tempo play, but I just found the whole thing uninteresting. I'd have to really force myself to care about this one.
